subject: Ecosystem: Partner SDK grace-period & provisional compatibility proposal
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@apextools.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK changes: request for extended grace period and roadmap sync

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the heads-up in the release notes about upcoming SDK surface changes. We reviewed the brief and ran an internal sweep across our integrations. The high-level impact: several customers using Apex’s Redwood-backed pipelines rely on the current SDK call patterns for token streaming and a bespoke retry behavior. If the planned breaking changes go live on the cadence listed, we estimate non-trivial regressions for ~40% of our managed customers.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood extend the grace period for the v1 -> v2 SDK/endpoint changes (we’re requesting an additional 120 days beyond your notice)?
- Is there a compatibility flag or compatibility shim you can provide so we can opt-in customers incrementally?
- Can we schedule a roadmap sync next week to align on rollout windows and a shared testing plan?

Attached is an impact matrix that maps which Apex products and customer tiers will be affected (apex_sdk_impact_matrix.xlsx). We can share usage numbers for the top 10 customers if that helps prioritize.

We appreciate Redwood’s openness on deprecations—this is primarily to avoid a broad customer support load and unplanned change management.

Best,
Carlos
Director, Integrations
Apex Tools

---
Attachment: apex_sdk_impact_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub; columns: product, endpoints, avg monthly calls, customer_count, estimated_breakage)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@apextools.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK changes: request for extended grace period and roadmap sync

Carlos — thanks for the detailed note and the impact matrix. Really helpful context.

High-level response: we want to avoid forcing breaking churn on our partner ecosystem, so we’re open to a measured compromise. Before we commit we need:
- A short list (top 5) of exact SDK calls/endpoints that would break for Apex and the estimated customer impact per call (if you can give us rough monthly call volumes that’s ideal).
- Any timeline constraints driven by your customers (e.g., contract renewals, major releases) so we can align dates.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync next Tue or Wed (30min) — Vanessa will bring product nuance; Karthik will assess engineering gating needs.
2) We’ll draft two options for you: 90-day and 180-day grace windows plus a compatibility-flag approach that lets partners opt into the new behavior on a per-account basis.
3) If the shim is feasible, we’ll include an offer of 48h of dedicated migration support and a small usage credit to cover regression testing.

Can you confirm availability for a 30min slot next Tue/Wed and attach the top-5 impacted calls? I’ll put a calendar invite together.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@apextools.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK changes: request for extended grace period and roadmap sync

Soojin — thanks, we’re available. Wed 04/07 at 10:00 PT works for our team. I’ve attached a short migration estimate and a breakdown of the top 5 failing patterns (apex_migration_estimates.pdf). Summary below:

Top impacted patterns (short):
- streaming.streamTokens() — uses legacy framing; needs new framing header (estimated 3 dev-weeks)
- client.retryBackoff() — behavior change in v2; needs shim for exponential cap (2 dev-weeks)
- embeddings.batchSend() — argument order change; tests only (1 dev-week)
- auth.refreshToken() — minor; dependent on infra rollout (2 dev-days)
- response.metadataKey rename — easy patch (3 dev-days)

Estimates above assume we can run against a Redwood staging instance and that any compatibility flag is available. If you can offer a 120–180 day soft window and a compatibility toggle, we can sequence our rollout so only high-risk customers migrate after adequate testing.

We’ll join the Wed invite.

—Carlos
Attachment: apex_migration_estimates.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@apextools.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed cadence: provisional compatibility + staged sunset (draft)

Carlos & team — great sync yesterday. Below is a concrete proposal from Product + Eng that aims to balance partner stability and our roadmap cadence. We want this to be actionable so your PM/legal teams can comment quickly.

Proposal (three pillars):
1) Notice & Documentation (Immediate)
   - 2027-05-15: Public deprecation notice for legacy SDK patterns (formal doc + migration guide).
2) Provisional Compatibility Flag (Opt-in)
   - 2027-05-15 -> 2027-11-15 (6 months): Introduce a compatibility flag on the Redwood API and SDKs: ?compat=legacy=true that preserves legacy framing/retries for flagged accounts. This will be toggled on a per-account basis by support/partner team.
   - Mechanism: compatibility flag implemented at the gateway layer; SDKs will accept a flag and route accordingly.
3) Sunset & Hard Cut
   - 2027-11-15: Remove legacy behavior; flag becomes unavailable.

Support & Compensation:
- Engineering support: up to 3 dedicated migration days from Redwood engineering for Apex (staging access + triage).
- Commercial: a one-time migration credit (equivalent to $5k USD) for Apex-managed customers that require additional testing cycles.
- Legal: we will prepare a short addendum (DocuSign) to document the extended cadence and responsibilities.

Attachments: redwood_deprecation_cadence.pdf (draft cadence + rollout playbook)
Relevant links: HubSpot record APX-7903, staging access request form.

Next asks for Apex:
- Confirm whether the 6-month window (May 15 -> Nov 15) is acceptable or if you need a longer run (we can consider an additional 60 days for specific enterprise customers via an opt-out extension process).
- Confirm contact for DocuSign addendum and staging credentials.

If this looks good we’ll route for legal and create a DocuSign addendum for signature.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: redwood_deprecation_cadence.pdf
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@apextools.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed cadence: provisional compatibility + staged sunset (draft)

Vanessa — appreciate the thoughtful proposal. The 6-month window + compatibility flag addresses most of our risks. Two quick asks before we sign the addendum:

1) Can Redwood issue test credentials for a dedicated Apex staging tenant by 2027-04-20 so we can start validating streaming.streamTokens and retryBackoff under the flag?
2) For two enterprise customers with renewal windows in August, can we request an opt-out extension until 2027-01-15-2028 (i.e., Redwood would allow legacy behavior for those two accounts until Jan 15 2028) documented in the addendum as carve-outs?

If you can accommodate staging access and carve-outs for those two accounts we’ll route the addendum for signatures this week. Otherwise, the plan looks good and we appreciate the migration credit and engineering support.

Thanks — will await the staging link.

—Carlos
